dimensions.title: Cognitive
milestones: Can solve simple puzzles and problems
Understands the concept of time and can tell time
Begins to think logically about concrete events
activities: Play board games that require strategy
Engage in simple science experiments
Encourage storytelling to enhance problem-solving

dimensions.title: Language
milestones: Can read simple books independently
Uses complex sentences and varied vocabulary
Engages in conversations and can express thoughts clearly
activities: Read together daily and discuss the story
Encourage writing short stories or journal entries
Play word games like Scrabble or Boggle

dimensions.title: Physical
milestones: Rides a bicycle with confidence
Can catch and throw a ball effectively
Shows improved hand-eye coordination
activities: Join a sports team or group activity
Practice activities like jumping rope or dancing
Engage in arts and crafts that require fine motor skills
watchFor: Inability to engage in age-appropriate physical activities
Fatigue or frustration during physical play

dimensions.title: Social
milestones: Enjoys playing with peers and forming friendships
Understands the concept of sharing and cooperation
Can empathize with feelings of others
activities: Organize playdates or group games
Encourage team sports
Engage in role-playing games to enhance social skills

dimensions.title: Emotional
milestones: Begins to understand and express their own emotions
Shows empathy and can comfort peers
Develops coping strategies for frustrations
activities: Practice emotion identification through games
Encourage sharing feelings during family discussions
Provide opportunities for role-playing complex emotional situations

dimensions.title: Curiosity
milestones: Asks a variety of questions about their environment
Shows interest in how things work
Enjoys exploring new ideas and concepts
activities: Visit museums or science centers
Encourage outdoor exploration and nature walks
Provide kits for building or experimenting at home
watchFor: Lack of interest in learning new things

dimensions.title: Learning
milestones: Can focus on tasks for longer periods
Uses strategies to remember information
Shows persistence in completing projects
activities: Set up a daily routine to encourage focus
Introduce problem-solving games that require persistence
Encourage participation in learning clubs or groups
watchFor: Gives up quickly when faced with challenges

dimensions.title: Independence
milestones: Can complete basic self-care tasks independently
Takes responsibility for personal belongings
Makes simple decisions
activities: Assign age-appropriate chores
Encourage dressing and grooming independently
Involve them in family decision-making processes
watchFor: Over-reliance on adults for basic tasks
Lack of initiative in personal responsibilities
